His legal team filed a petition seeking the immediate return of the seized phone.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: US authorities seized James Chambers's cellphone from a Madrid court while he was imprisoned in Spain. Chambers's lawyer said the court secretly handed the phone to the FBI despite written guarantees it would remain in court custody until his extradition request was resolved.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Lawyers argue the seizure violates Spanish law, political asylum protections, and a 1970 US-Spain extradition treaty. This case is the first known attempt by the US to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Chambers's defence team has petitioned an appeals court for the phone's immediate return and an explanation. Spanish courts could take months to decide on the extradition request.
